requirements_summary: Workloads: secure assistant for ops teams + sensitive-document embeddings and reranking
Latency target: sub-200ms tail for short assistant queries (strict for incident ops)
Throughput: peak bursts ~200 QPS across 150 agents; steady-state lower
Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to pay premium for isolation and certified stack
Model preferences: Open-source Llama-family variants or vetted Red-team-evaluated models; ability to pin versions
Routing/fallback: must not fail open to public cloud; internal fallback to smaller local model
Compliance: absolute air-gapped isolation required (no egress), HSM-backed keys, 7+ year audit logs, on-prem appliance preferred
notes: Summary: Strong technical fit but lost to on-prem/appliance requirement. Aurora's SecOps will not accept a private deployment that requires outbound control-plane connectivity.
Key quote: 'We cannot tolerate any external control plane. If you need to talk to your cloud, it's a non-starter.' — Aurora SecOps lead

Engagement tone: cordial but rigid on security constraints. Multiple product workarounds discussed (air-gapped private control plane, shipped appliance), but timelines and engineering resources were blockers.
Why lost: competitor offered embedded appliance + onsite install + longer warranty; Aurora prioritized vendor who could provide physical isolation and on-site SLA.
Internal notes: no clear internal champion surfaced after pilot phase. Primary sponsor (Dir of Cyber Ops) rotated roles in Dec; procurement deprioritized due to budget freeze.
Follow-up guidance: Capture appliance feasibility notes and share with product strategy; flag for potential 2026 re-engagement if Redwood invests in appliance/air-gap offering.
